cells.tense: The result is here and you are standing in it with your hands open, not counting.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you made and let someone else use it their own way, without your instructions. Let it be theirs.
cells.core:
When the road isn't visible yet, you don't force a shape onto it. You take the step you can actually see, and that has been enough to bring something real through — something that now stands on its own. You can watch it work and not reach in.

That's this thing going well: growth that doesn't exhaust you, care that holds without clutching. You're not standing over the result, correcting it, or moving straight to the next. You let a thing be finished and let it be good. That ease is what lets what you grew belong to the people it reached, rather than staying a project of yours.
cells.sheetLine: What you grew is here, and you can let it be enough.
cells.verb: letting what was tended come in
cells.place: the room where the path shows itself one step at a time

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead the whole thing arrives, and you are braced for a future that cannot be written in yet.
cells.ask: Take one person's half-formed idea and sit with it until you feel what they mean. Don't fix it or improve it today.
cells.core:
You're living in a version of this that hasn't happened. The result is already here and you're still out ahead of it, planning next season, pulling a future into a present that doesn't need you to. From the outside it looks like care. From the inside it's a grip that will not let go.

What walking through uncertainty well looks like: enough light for one step, and the trust to take it. What you've got instead is a forecast for every step you haven't taken yet. Loosening that grip means joining one real thing in front of you — a person, an idea — rather than managing the ones you imagine. What you made doesn't need guarding.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying a result that hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, waiting for it to open again.
cells.ask: Name one direction you can actually see from where you stand and take one small step toward it this week.
cells.core:
What going well looks like here is simple: enough light for the next step, and the willingness to take it before the whole road is visible. Seeing everything isn't the requirement. Moving is. What you have instead is a wait — you stop at the edge of the unknown and hold still, because the way hasn't shown itself all at once, and it won't.

So the step doesn't get taken. What you tended is sitting there, finished or near it, and you stand off to one side like a visitor in a room you used to live in. The light hasn't gone anywhere. What's missing is a direction you've chosen out loud and the motion that follows it.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped taking steps into the not-knowing.

cells.tense: You are already in the middle of it, walking the not-knowing like it's nothing, and calling it luck.
cells.ask: Say out loud or write down: this one is mine. Name something you've been calling the way things went instead of your doing.
cells.core:
You move through not-knowing better than most people and don't clock it as a skill. You'd call it getting by, or being flexible, or just how it went. But the thing is running: you take the next visible step over and over without demanding the whole road first, and something real has grown from it. What that looks like going well is exactly what you're doing, minus the disclaimer.

The doing goes unattributed. You describe what came out of it as circumstance, as timing, as something that happened to you, instead of the thing you kept at while you couldn't see ahead. It's already yours. The only piece left is saying so — to yourself first, and then out loud to someone who was there.
cells.sheetLine: You're already walking the not-knowing. You call it luck.

attempts.check: The record says the seat is Imagination (navigating ambiguity) but the card is Spirit house, outer abundance — I render the seat as the place where the person walks in not-knowing, without importing anything about what they have or haven't built. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't experience my life as a garden at all' — the garden never enters the cell, only the plain fact that what was tended is now bearing. The asks survive a wrong read: leaving one thing alone, not finishing the sentence today, naming a direction from inside the fog, calling one thing yours — all useful even if the mechanism is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything about low light or half-seen roads as a mood; it stays out, or it stays as a fact of the weather.

At Too Little the medicine is Orientation (choosing a star) — so the ask must be about picking a direction, not about waiting for the fog to thin. A reader could reasonably say 'nothing I tended is bearing'; the plants stay out, and so does any word like harvest — the plain fact is that something has grown and is here. The asks survive a wrong read: leaving a thing running without you, joining one person's way of seeing, taking one visible step, putting a name on what you did. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about the fog as atmosphere; ambiguity stays a condition, not a mood.
